answer: AI agents cataloging walnut inks, violet dyes, and quill parchments resist Sybil attacks via graph-based trust networks. By routing validation tokens through bounded random walks on mutual interaction graphs, the protocol exploits structural bottlenecks to isolate fabricated clusters. Attackers must expend scarce social capital and historical interaction time to establish genuine trust edges per node. A core limitation is that honest newcomer agents suffer severe cold-start isolation.
